evidence: Built a requirement -> criterion map from instruction.md and both notes against 2 gate + 43 functional + 5 polish + 5 visual criteria. Nearly everything maps: one-stage moves and non-drag controls (hro_move_one_stage, hro_reorder, hro_reject_reason, hro_reopen, hro_bulk_move); shared order (hro_reorder, hro_arrive_bottom); Interview places (hro_interview_full, hro_interview_reorder_free, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_full); refused put-back + reason + focus (hro_refused_put_back); stale move + who (hro_stale_refused); all-or-none (hro_bulk_all_or_none); undo rules (hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once, reason restored in hro_reopen); live board within 15 s (hro_live_board) and preservation of open card, typed note, focus and scroll (hro_pol_live_board); latest 30 / earlier paging / place kept (hro_thread_latest, hro_thread_earlier, hro_pol_earlier_place); scrolled-up arrival notice (hro_unread_scrolled_up); draft and cursor kept on arrival (hro_pol_live_thread); per-person unread and total incl. seeded read marker (hro_unread_counts); seen incl. observer exclusion (hro_seen); drafts across conversations, board and reload (hro_drafts) and across session end and another user on the same browser, incl. unsaved note drafts (hro_pol_session_resume); failed send (hro_pol_failed_send); Enter/Shift+Enter/empty+focused (hro_msg_compose); candidate wording, own applications, privacy, 404 (hro_candidate_view, hro_candidate_private, hro_candidate_linked); roles (hro_mgr_late_stages, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous with 401); intake and email rules (hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_add_email_rules); activity, filter, refusals (hro_activity, hro_activity_refusals); notes (hro_notes); seed once and persistence (hro_restart); clear desktop workspace (visual). 'Signing in does not open a conversation' is indirectly covered (an auto-open would break Lena's 1 unread in Z and the not-yet-seen leg of hro_seen). GAP (credible, ungraded): server-side conversation write/read authorization. hireops_rules.md:131-134 states 'A hiring manager can read and write only in conversations of their own jobs; the others are refused', 'The observer can read every conversation and write in none', 'A candidate can read and write only in their own'; :21-23 requires session-based 403/404 server refusals. But hro_thread_access (functional/judge.toml:357-363) accepts 'a manager of another job (Ingrid) cannot open it (not listed, or refused)' and 'the Observer reads it and cannot send (no send control, or a send is refused with nothing added)', and protocol T (functional/prompt.md:39) says 'as Ingrid ... check it is not available or refused; as Aud read it and confirm no way to send' - not 'try' steps, so no replay is mandated. hro_observer_readonly (:168-174) replays only 'move, add-candidate, open-job and note' - no message request. hro_candidate_no_staff (:177-183) also omits messages, and hro_candidate_private (:384-390) replays only a READ of another application's conversation ('asking for another application's conversation is answered as not found'), never a send. So server refusal of message writes by the Observer, by another job's manager and by a candidate into someone else's conversation, and server refusal of another job's manager reading the conversation, go ungraded whenever the UI hides the control - inconsistent with the task's own stated principle for role rules ('what is graded is that the server refuses it', functional/prompt.md:23) that every board and note role check follows. The golden enforces it (solution/app/src/index.js:116,127-128 return 403/404), so the check is feasible. Residual lower-severity partial gaps, reported because the row asks for every gap: (a) rules :21 '403' for role refusals is never required (criteria accept any refusal; only 401 is status-checked, in hro_anonymous) - P3; (b) instruction.md:3 'tell me who' and rules :79-80 'The person is told ... by whom, and their board shows the card where it really is' - hro_stale_refused accepts the name 'in the response or on screen' after a fetch replay, so a UI that never displays who changed the card is ungraded; a reasoned feasibility tradeoff because push-based apps cannot be put into a stale UI state, Note level; (c) rules :98 undo refused if a card was 'reopened since' - hro_undo_conflict exercises moved, re-ordered and rejected but not reopened (e.g. Rafael rejects, Mei reopens, Rafael undoes) - P3; (d) rules :84 'A move appears on the mover's board immediately' and integration.md 'GET /api/health answers before database work' are not judge-graded (the latter belongs to test.sh liveness / runtime contract, not judge criteria) - Note. This is a source-coverage row; no runtime evidence was required or claimed, and no Oracle, model or portal score is implied.
counterexample: Broken app that should lose credit but earns full marks on every row touching conversation access: the UI hides the message box for the Observer and lists only own-job conversations for a hiring manager, but POST and GET /api/applications/:id/messages only check that a session exists (no role, job or ownership check). Aud can post into any conversation through the API, Ingrid can read and write J2 conversations, and Tomas can post into Noor's conversation by id. hro_thread_access passes ('no send control' / 'not listed'), hro_observer_readonly and hro_candidate_no_staff pass (no message replay), and hro_candidate_private passes (only the GET of another conversation is replayed; a separate GET handler can 404 while the POST succeeds). The stated rule 'The observer can read every conversation and write in none' is violated with no deduction.
suggested_fix: Make the Observer's send, Ingrid's J2 conversation read and send, and Tomas's send into an application that is not his into 'try' steps that replay Rafael's captured message requests in those sessions, required in hro_thread_access to be refused with nothing added, with Rafael's and Bill's successful sends as the controls.
